body_markdown:
After building the audacious M1 in 1978, BMW’s move to performance sedans was a lot more subdued. While the later E30 M3 of 1986 would feature stylish fender flares and a sizable rear wing, both the M535i, which debuted in 1980, and the brand’s first M5, launched in 1985, kept their increased performance under wraps. Aside from color-matched mirrors, a subtle front air dam, and a couple of emblems, onlookers would have little to differentiate BMW’s driver-focused M5 from an average, 2.0-liter executive car.


RPF Motorcars


RPF Motorcars


The U.S.-spec M5, which arrived as a 1988 model, was powered by a 3.5-liter S38 inline-six with Bosch Motronic fuel injection, and the cars featured a Getrag five-speed manual transmission. Run-of-the-mill BMW inline-six engines of the era used a single overhead camshaft and two valves per cylinder, but the S38 used dual overhead cams and four valves per cylinder. Breathing through six throttle bodies, it produced 256 horsepower at 6500 rpm. While buyers in other markets had 20 exterior color options, U.S. buyers could have their M5 in any color they wanted, as long as it was Jet Black.


RPF Motorcars


Only about 2200 E28 M5s were built, making them one of the rarest of all regular-production BMWs. That rarity, combined with their understated styling and responsive handling, makes the E28 M5 one of the most collectible of all BMW performance sedans. We’ve seen[well-preserved, low-mileage examples](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/low-miles-big-price-for-record-breaking-196k-bmw-e28-m5/) bring big numbers at auction.


[This 1988 M5](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/1988-BMW-M5/3690ef87-2039-422a-8fc1-739b21d482d4) , with 135,100 miles on the odometer, is currently up for bid on Hagerty Marketplace. Since it does have six digits’ worth of mileage on the clock, we’re not expecting this one to shatter any records. Nevertheless, the car is loaded with the features you’d expect from a 1980s European luxury sport sedan. All E28 M5s came equipped with four-wheel disc brakes with ABS, air conditioning, a power sunroof, a limited-slip differential, cruise control, and power windows and door locks. This one in particular also has some nice OEM-plus and day-two modifications, including upgraded brakes from an E81 8 Series, H&R lowering springs, and a set of 17-inch BMW Style 19 wheels from BBS. We don’t miss the factory wheels. Not because of their style, but because they were sized for Michelin’s low-profile TRX tires. Now it’s ready for a wider range of performance rubber.


While European-spec M5s featured the M88/3 inline-six derived from the mid-engine M1 that produced 288 horsepower, the U.S.-spec S38 was down a bit of power, but it was newer and cleaner. And its 256 horsepower was still significantly more than the 182 hp from the 535i and M535i that were the next in the E28 pecking order.


RPF Motorcars


This Northern California car has clearly been kept in tip-top shape. It has plenty of service records and a recent California emissions test to prove it. Its most significant refresh came in 2023 at SEA Works in Rancho Cordova, California. It received a major paint refinishing with new weatherstripping, rear bumper fillers, and new hood and decklid emblems. The car will be available to view in person at[RADwood NorCal](https://www.radwood.com/) on Saturday, October 24, and bidding ends the 26th.


RPF Motorcars


Right about now, it’s on its way to Alameda, California, to be on display at[RADwood NorCal](https://www.radwood.com/) . Potential bidders on site can look it over in person. Admission is free. Even if you’re not in the market, you can get a good look for yourself and take in some ‘80s and ‘90s car culture where this M5 will be among its peers.
